newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Surgical says Q1 revs hurt by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Surgical says Q1 revs hurt by strong dollar.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp said a strong dollar will pressure its first quarter revenues, but its earnings will meet Wall Street expectations.

U.S. Surgical spokeswoman Marianne Scipione said the company agreed with a Cowen & Co report that suggested U.S. Surgical would report lighter-than-expected first quarter revenue growth due to the strong dollar.

The company did not provide specific revenue expectations but said it is comfortable with analysts' consensus earnings estimate of $0.37 a share. The company earned $0.28 a share last year, according to First Call.
Cowen analyst Daniel Lemaitre reiterated a buy rating on U.S. Surgical, Scipione said. Lemaitre could not be reached for comment.
U.S. Surgical, which makes surgical staplers, endoscopic devices and sutures, lost 3-7/8 to 39-3/8.
